[[slide:greeting]]
Hi Morgan. This is a short recap of your 2025 federal, Kansas, and Missouri income tax returns, filed as head of household. We will cover what you earned, what you paid in during the year, and where the refund came from.
[[slide:income]]
Your total income was $71,805. Almost all of it was wages of $71,300, with taxable interest of $95 and dividends of $410 making up the rest.
[[slide:deductions]]
With no adjustments to income, your adjusted gross income was $71,805. The standard deduction of $22,500 brought your taxable income down to $49,305.
[[slide:tax]]
The income tax on that amount was $5,100. A child tax credit of $2,000 reduced it to a total federal tax of $3,100, which is an effective rate of 6.3% on your taxable income.
[[slide:result]]
You paid in $6,400 through withholding, and refundable credits added another $1,600, for total payments of $8,000. That is well above your total tax, so the return shows a federal refund of $4,900. Kansas, your resident state, also came out in your favor: state tax of $2,150 against state withholding of $2,400 leaves a Kansas refund of $250. Missouri went the other way, with a small state balance due of $120.
[[slide:observations]]
Your withholding covered 206.5% of your total tax, which is why the federal refund was so large. In plain terms, a good part of each paycheck went to the government during the year and is only coming back to you now.
[[slide:next]]
A complete copy of both returns is being delivered to you with this summary, so you have every form and schedule for your records. Everything you just heard comes straight from those pages. If any part of it is unclear, our office is glad to walk you through it. Please contact us with any questions.
